result.title: LEGOSpec: A Composable and Efficient Framework for Speculative Draft Design and Training
result.comment: 11 pages. Code and weights are available at the URL in the paper
result.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) generation using a lightweight draft. Existing methods evaluate complete recipes under different training configurations, leaving component effects, interactions, and composition benefits unclear. Therefore, we present LEGOSpec, a composable framework for speculative draft design and training. LEGOSpec decomposes draft models into Context, Backbone, Proposal, and Objective components that share a unified training infrastructure. Using LEGOSpec, we systematically vary components and evaluate selected combinations under matched training conditions to isolate their effects and interactions. These experiments reveal three findings: (1) Different workloads favor different backbones, depending on context length and memory budget, with within-block dependency modeling particularly important for long contexts. (2) Proposal design must balance acceptance and latency. (3) The training objective should match token distributions locally and optimize acceptance length across the block. These findings guide workload-aware configurations and DFlux, a balanced general-purpose draft combining a convolution-equipped SWA--GQA hybrid backbone, Residual Corrector, and hierarchical supervision. Across Qwen and Gemma models, DFlux improves acceptance length over the strongest baseline by up to 13.7% on regular benchmarks and 34.7% on long-context workloads. To support efficient training, LEGOSpec integrates metadata-aware scheduling and asynchronous execution, increasing training throughput by up to 79% and accelerating offline supervision preparation by up to $3.11\times$ over SpecForge.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 LEGOSpec，将投机解码的 draft 模型拆成 Context、Backbone、Proposal、Objective 四个可组合组件并在统一训练框架下做匹配条件的对照实验，据此给出面向负载的配置建议和组合式 draft 模型 DFlux，同时优化训练调度与离线监督准备效率。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文本身面向 LLM 解码加速而非视觉推理，但其「一次预测多 token 并由主模型校验」的块内依赖建模、Residual Corrector 与按接受长度设计的层级监督，可供核查是否能迁移到 latent 推理状态的逐步提议与更新。
